questions.question: Q1. What is the primary objective of the Experiment 3 simulation?

answers.a: To monitor solar cell generation and grid power quality
answers.b: To study bidirectional Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) energy exchange under automated state machine transitions
answers.c: To test the physical structural durability of EV charging cables
answers.d: To manually stabilize frequency fluctuations in an islanded microgrid

explanations.a: Solar generation is not part of this simulation's objective.
explanations.b: The objective section explicitly states the experiment is designed to study bidirectional V2G and G2V energy exchange with automated state transitions.
explanations.c: Cable durability is a mechanical characteristic not covered by this software simulation.
explanations.d: Frequency stabilization is not the stated focus of this experiment.

questions.question: Q2. What specific battery State of Charge (SOC) safety threshold triggers the BMS Safety Override Alert?

explanations.a: 20% is the lower limit of the SOC slider, not the override trigger point.
explanations.b: 35% is not mentioned in the safety protocols.
explanations.c: The safety alert banner text explicitly states that the BMS override activates when the battery reaches the 50% SOC safety threshold.
explanations.d: 80% is a typical charging limit but does not trigger the override banner in this file.

questions.question: Q3. When the BMS Safety Override becomes active, what automatic adjustment is made to the substation demand?

answers.a: Discharging is suspended and switched to charging (G2V) mode
answers.b: The inverter AC voltage is boosted to 260 V
answers.c: The system enters a full physical disconnect state automatically
answers.d: Current is increased to maximum to drain the battery faster

explanations.a: The override banner states that discharging is suspended and the system switches to charging (G2V) mode to maintain safety thresholds.
explanations.b: Voltage modifications are performed via the slider, not by the BMS override.
explanations.c: The system stays connected but switches modes rather than fully disconnecting.
explanations.d: Draining the battery further would violate the safety threshold constraint.

questions.question: Q4. Which of the following equations represents the Governing Relation displayed in the controls panel?

explanations.a: Dividing voltage by current does not yield electrical power.
explanations.b: The Governing Relation panel clearly shows the power formula as P = V × I.
explanations.c: While valid as Ohm's Law, this is not the governing formula shown in this layout.
explanations.d: This relates to resistive power loss and is not the relationship featured in the UI panel.

questions.question: Q5. What are the allowed minimum and maximum configuration limits for the Inverter AC Voltage slider?

explanations.a: These voltages are too low for typical standard AC inverter simulations.
explanations.b: These are common household values but do not match the UI limits configured here.
explanations.c: The voltage HTML input element explicitly specifies a min of 180 and a max of 260.
explanations.d: These values exceed the operational constraints of this specific single-phase configuration.

questions.question: Q6. What is the default initial setting of the EV State of Charge (SOC) slider before user adjustment?

explanations.a: 20% represents the minimum selectable slider limit.
explanations.b: 50% represents the threshold where the override activates.
explanations.c: The HTML input attributes define the default starting value as 90%.
explanations.d: 100% is the maximum bound of the charging range.

questions.question: Q7. Which metric from the top telemetry bar displays the actual power exchanged after accounting for efficiency factors?

explanations.a: Calculated power represents the theoretical input calculation before efficiency losses.
explanations.b: Grid target is the reference expectation set by the utility system.
explanations.c: Inverter temperature is a thermal indicator, not a power metric.
explanations.d: Net Transferred Power reflects the actual energy successfully transferred through the bidirectional link.

questions.question: Q8. What button text indicates the initial step a user must take to start the synchronization process?

explanations.a: Reset Bench re-initializes parameters to original defaults.
explanations.b: The primary action button initializes with the text 'Position Cable to Begin' to guide the physical connection phase.
explanations.c: This button is initially disabled and used to terminate an active connection.
explanations.d: Clear Records empties the logged data table without impacting connection state.

questions.question: Q9. What happens if a user adjusts the Discharging Current slider to its maximum allowable limit?

explanations.a: 5 A represents the absolute minimum boundary of the current slider.
explanations.b: 20 A is the default loaded value, not the maximum configuration.
explanations.c: The slider input properties establish a maximum current value boundary of 60 A.
explanations.d: 100 A is beyond the parameters defined inside this simulation layout.

questions.question: Q10. According to the default layout, what condition tells the user that no telemetric tracking records have been generated yet?

answers.a: The sync status badge reads 'DISCONNECTED' and a table row states 'No telemetry records logged'
answers.c: The inverter temperature drops instantly to 0 °C

explanations.a: The template includes an empty-row placeholder in the table body instructing users to adjust sliders and synchronize to begin logging telemetry records.
explanations.b: The 3D environment retains its background independent of telemetry history logging.
explanations.c: The standard resting temperature is hardcoded at an initial 25.0 °C.
explanations.d: The governing math relation banner remains statically visible for reference.
